style.vernacular: Hillside highland capital at about 1,000 m: a colonial core of whitewashed and pastel (salmon, ochre) adobe and masonry buildings with red Spanish clay-tile roofs and Baroque churches; two-storey buildings until the 1980s, then concrete avenues, overpasses and blocks; dense hillside colonias of painted concrete-block houses under corrugated metal roofs; glass-and-render malls and towers on the ridges; pine and oak on the surrounding hills.
style.ornament: Baroque church fronts with Solomonic columns and bell towers; colonial arcaded portals and wooden balconies with iron grilles; painted pastel facade bands; hillside walls with painted murals; red-tile eaves; wrought-iron window grilles on almost every house.

sources.what: hilly valley city, two-storey buildings until the 1980s, colonial cathedral 1765 and churches, pine and oak hills, hillside poorer neighbourhoods, high-rise and malls on ridges
Baroque, salmon-coloured exterior restored, 60 x 11 x 18 m with a 30 m dome
